plan_prompt:
## Settled design (the planner grounds it; nobody re-derives it)

1. DESIGN-EXTENSIONS.md: a component declaration carries shape + view +
   ACTIONS + schedule. K6 (declared faces, landed manifold e58973d) built the
   view half; this leg builds the actions half the SAME way.
2. K6 precedent, ruled at ROUND-20260813-VIEW-EYES-WORKFLOWS.md r1.2 and now
   proven in the tree: capability declarations travel as RECORD ENTRIES on
   the registry feed, never code; a closed v1 vocabulary grows only by core
   release; carried implementations win over declared ones for their tokens.
3. K8 DELIVERY MODEL — ruled here (Waffles, 2026-08-14, extending the K6
   precedent under Tom's 2026-08-12 technical delegation):
   - Actions travel as a new facet `manifold.facet.actions@v1` on the
     component declaration. Body: `{ "actions": { "<kind-token>":
     [ <action>... ] } }`. Unknown facets already travel verbatim — the core
     needs NO change (⛔ STOP-REPORT if any crates/ change seems required).
   - An action is one of exactly TWO closed v1 primitives:
     * `{ "primitive": "respond", "label": "<literal>",
        "kind": "<record-kind-token>", "body": { ...literal template... } }`
       — ONE control; pressing it IS the act (Tom's click-is-the-act ruling):
       it sends a signed record entry of the declared kind through the
       page's EXISTING write door, body = the declared literal template plus
       a reference to the acted-on entry. No composer detour.
     * `{ "primitive": "choose", "from": "<list-field>",
        "kind": "<record-kind-token>" }` — one control PER ITEM of the
       acted-on record's list field; pressing an item sends a signed entry
       of the declared kind carrying that item plus the reference. This is
       the vote shape, generalized.
   - deny-unknown-fields at every level; unknown primitive names or missing
     members are MALFORMED and refuse BY NAME (the declared-face refusal
     register). A `choose` over a non-list value refuses that action,
     renders the rest.
   - The act routes through the page's existing write path ONLY. No write
     path for the room ⇒ the control renders disabled with the refusal in
     words (the exact precedent of the poll vote refusal in mount.ts). The
     ownership of signing, sequencing, and delivery stays with the existing
     door — this leg adds ZERO new wire surface.
   - CARRIED-WINS: poll's hand-wired vote path is the carried specimen and
     is NOT rewired. ⛔ poll-face.ts and poll.ts untouched. Unifying poll
     onto the general path is a later leg, exactly as poll's face stayed
     hand-wired in K6 leg 1.
   - The K7/K8 fork (per-message action vs whole-room palette verb) is
     TOM'S question and stays OPEN — this leg builds only the per-message
     arm he already asked for. Nothing here forecloses K7.

## Leg topology (FAN-OUT r1.1: parallel legs, isolated worktrees, disjoint
## file zones — Tom's fan-out ruling 2026-08-14; each brief fully
## self-contained, no leg sees another's work, branches merged mechanically)

- **L1 `schema-red`** — OWNS: the new composition cases file
  (scripts/composition-declared-action-cases.mjs), its registration in
  composition-test.mjs, the fixture records/rsvp-declaration.json, and
  gate-logs/declared-actions/red.log. Content: the fixture kind
  `ablative.message.rsvp@v1` (fields: `prompt` text, `options` text-list)
  declared with renders + accepts + face + ACTIONS facets beside the
  existing fixtures, and the RED: cases asserting derivation, control
  shape, refusal-by-name, and the choose-over-non-list refusal against
  the vocabulary ruled above — committed FAILING with the red run's
  output as evidence in the leg's own commit. The red is red-first BY
  CONSTRUCTION of the fan: green exists only on the merged tree, never
  in this leg. Report to .fleet/reports/L1.md.
- **L2 `derive-build`** — OWNS: the new derivation module (one new file
  under surface/page/src, ≤500 LOC, house style of declared-face.ts) and
  the mount.ts composition seam. Content: per-kind action rosters derived
  from mounted declarations per the ruled vocabulary, composed
  carried-first at the mount seam; controls rendered on the rendered
  kind; a press routes through the existing write path; no-write-path
  renders disabled-with-words. Written against the RULED vocabulary in
  this brief (not against L1's cases, which this leg never sees). Report
  to .fleet/reports/L2.md.

The MERGED tree is where L1's red turns green — the gates prove it
mechanically after fanin. The dev-estate browser walk (declared rsvp
renders choose controls, press produces a signed entry on the feed,
refusal-in-words on the no-write-path room, dist bytes untouched) moves
to the DISPATCHER'S re-gate desk before landing, where a composed page
exists to walk — a pre-merge isolated tree cannot walk a composition.

## Hard walls (restated in every leg brief by the planner)

⛔ Live estate untouchable: ports 4176/41100/41101/41102/9490s, every
.manifold* path — dev estates only. ⛔ No crates/ changes (STOP-REPORT).
⛔ No vendor/ edits, no import-map changes, no new served files, no dynamic
import() — code delivery is refused by settled design. ⛔ poll-face.ts +
poll.ts untouched. ⛔ No lint bypasses, no test skips. ⛔ Existing pinned
cases byte-untouched — a pin conflict is a STOP-REPORT, never a rewrite.
Worktree only; never land, merge, push, or deploy — Waffles re-gates the
final tree and lands.

You are the PLANNER of a fleet run. Your working directory is the target repository worktree. Write .fleet/plan.md (the whole plan, every requirement anchored file:line into THIS tree) and one complete builder brief per leg at .fleet/legs/L1.md and .fleet/legs/L2.md. The legs will run IN PARALLEL, each builder in its own isolated worktree on its own branch — no leg sees another leg's work, and the branches are merged mechanically afterwards. Each brief must therefore be fully self-contained and independent of the other legs' outputs, and must name exactly which files its leg owns so no two legs write the same file; if the settled design forces two legs toward the same file, say so explicitly in .fleet/plan.md and assign that file to exactly one leg. Each brief is floors-not-ceilings, anchored, restates the hard walls above, and names the report file the builder must write (.fleet/reports/<id>.md). You are planning CONTENT for this fixed topology, not changing it. Commit nothing; the .fleet/ files are your only writes. When done, reply with a short summary of the plan you wrote.
